newsitem.title: EGYPT: Russia says Mideast peace to stay on Madrid track.
newsitem.headline: Russia says Mideast peace to stay on Madrid track.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov said on Wednesday his country would do its utmost to keep the Middle East peace process on the same track the Arabs and Israelis agreed upon in a 1991 Madrid peace conference.

"There must be an awareness that Russia will carry on its efforts to ensure the continuation of the principles and agreements that have been reached," Primakov told reporters after he met his Egyptian counterpart Amr Moussa.
A Russian envoy had said earlier that Primakov would visit the region armed with many initiatives to revive the flagging peace process but the minister would not say what they were.
"All efforts must be made for the negotiations to continue based on what is agreed on," he said when asked about the initiatives. "We will do our utmost to push the peace process in that direction."

The Russian foreign minister arrived in Egypt on Wednesday on a Middle East tour intended to boost Russia's role as a co-sponsor of the peace process which was launched in Madrid in 1991 on the basis on exchaning Israeli-occupied Arab land for peace. The United States is the other main sponsor.
Primakov is also expected to hold talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in the Sinai resort of Sharm el-Sheikh later on Wednesday.
Palestinian-Israel peace talks are deadlocked over a promised Israeli troop redeployment from Hebron, the last West Bank town to be handed over to the Palestinians.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who was elected in May on a platform that opposes handing over occupied Arab lands for peace, is trying to renegotiate the deal to guarantee the security of Jewish settlers living there.
"The time now calls for all efforts to be taken to return the peace process to its track within the Madrid land-for-peace framework," Moussa told the news conference.
Primakov has already held talks with Syrian and Lebanese officials and will also visit Jordan, Israel and the Palestinian self-rule territories.
